subject: math
cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
intro: Geometry starts from a few undefined terms, point, line, and plane, that we describe but do not define. From these we build precise definitions. A point marks a location and has no size. A line extends forever in two directions and has no thickness. A line segment is the part of a line between two endpoints. An angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint (the vertex). A circle is the set of all points a fixed distance (the radius) from a center. Two lines are parallel if they lie in the same plane and never meet; they are perpendicular if they meet at a right angle ($90°$).

items.prompt: Define a line segment using the undefined term 'line'.

steps: Start from the undefined term line, which extends forever in both directions.
Pick two points on the line; call them the endpoints.
The line segment is the part of the line between and including those two endpoints.
solution.answer: A line segment is the part of a line between two endpoints, including the endpoints.

items.prompt: Two rays share the endpoint $V$. What figure do they form, and what is $V$ called?

steps: Two rays with a common endpoint form an angle.
The shared endpoint is the vertex of the angle.
So the rays form an angle with vertex $V$.
solution.answer: They form an angle; $V$ is the vertex.

items.prompt: A circle has center $O$ and radius $5$. Describe which points lie on the circle.

steps: A circle is the set of all points a fixed distance from a center.
Here the fixed distance (radius) is $5$ and the center is $O$.
So the circle is all points exactly $5$ units from $O$.
solution.answer: All points exactly $5$ units from the center $O$.

items.prompt: What does it mean for two lines to be perpendicular?

steps: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
solution.answer: They intersect at a right angle ($90°$).

items.prompt: What does it mean for two lines in a plane to be parallel?

steps: Parallel lines lie in the same plane.
They never intersect, no matter how far they are extended.
solution.answer: They lie in the same plane and never intersect.

items.prompt: Name the three undefined terms that geometry is built from.

steps: Geometry begins from terms we describe but do not define.
These are point, line, and plane.
